facts.statement: Dadagavialis was first described by scientists in 2018.
This extinct crocodilian lived during the Early Miocene in the region that is now Panama.
facts.quote: Dadagavialis is an extinct monospecific genus of gavialid crocodylian that lived during the Early Miocene in what is now Panama

facts.statement: When described, Dadagavialis was proposed to belong to the subfamily Gryposuchinae.
facts.quote: It was described in 2018, and was proposed to be a member of Gryposuchinae

facts.statement: Some researchers argue that Dadagavialis should be classified directly within Gavialidae because Gryposuchinae is considered an evolutionary grade rather than a distinct clade.
facts.quote: However, other studies have shown Gryposuchinae to be paraphyletic and rather an evolutionary grade towards the living gharial, and thus Dadagavialis might just be classified as a member of Gavialidae

facts.statement: Fossils of this species were found in the Cucaracha Formation of Panama, which dates to the Early Miocene.
facts.quote: Su registro fue encontrado en la Formación Cucaracha de Panamá que es del Mioceno temprano

facts.statement: During the Early Miocene, central Panama formed the southernmost part of the North American continent, bordering the Central American Seaway.
facts.quote: la parte central de Panamá fue la parte más austral del continente norteamericano en el Mioceno temprano, bordeando el estrecho de Centroamérica

facts.statement: Dadagavialis is a Gryposuchine gavialoid, a subfamily of gavials that was primarily found in South America.
facts.quote: Es un gavialoide griposuquino, una subfamilia de gaviales principalmente sudamericanos

facts.statement: Dadagavialis is distinguished from all other gavialoids by having a prefrontal process that is wider than the prefrontal bone at the level of the anterior orbital margin.
facts.quote: Se diferencia de todos los demás gavialoides por poseer un proceso anterior frontal más ancho que el prefrontal en el nivel del margen orbital anterior

facts.statement: The holotype of Dadagavialis gunai consists of a partial skull preserving a section of the snout, part of the cranial vault, and a partial neurocranium.
facts.quote: El holotipo de Dadagavialis gunai es un cráneo parcial que conserva una sección del hocico, parte de la bóveda craneana y un neurocráneo parcial

facts.statement: The genus name combines the Guna word "dada" for "ancient" with the Greek word "gavialis".
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva de la palabra "dada", de la lengua guna (lengua indígena en Panamá y Colombia) para "antiguo", y del griego "gavialis"

facts.statement: The species name "gunai" honors the Guna people, who are known as enthusiastic navigators of the Caribbean.
facts.quote: el nombre de la especie "gunai" para honrar a la gente Guna, conocida como navegantes entusiastas del Caribe

facts.statement: The parent group for Dadagavialis is the family Gavialidae.
Dadagavialis lived between 18.5 and 16.3 million years ago during the Burdigalian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Burdigalian to Burdigalian (18.5 to 16.3 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Dadagavialis gunai existed approximately 19 million years ago in the Caribbean region.
rejected.quote: Dadagavialis gunai es un género y especie extintos de reptiles crocodilianos gaviálidos que existió hace aproximadamente diecinueve millones de años en la zona del Caribe

rejected.statement: Within its group, Dadagavialis is a relatively small genus characterized by having more than 22 maxillary alveoli.
rejected.quote: Entre su grupo es un género relativamente pequeño diagnosticado, entre otras características, por presentar más de veintidós alvéolos maxilares
